tool.name: MIC-50-90 distribution bounds
tool.command: #if $source.type == 'json': ln -s '$source.distribution' input.json && #set $main_input = 'input.json' #else: ln -s '$source.summaries' input.csv && ln -s '$source.panels' panels.csv && #set $main_input = 'input.csv' #if $source.additional_counts: ln -s '$source.additional_counts' additional_counts.csv && #end if #end if #if $targets: ln -s '$targets' targets.csv && #end if mic-50-90 distribution '$main_input' #if $source.type == 'csv': --panels panels.csv #if $source.additional_counts: --additional-counts additional_counts.csv #end if --delimiter comma #end if #if $targets: --targets targets.csv #end if --population-method '$population.method' --population-time-limit $population.time_limit #if str($precision_pp): --precision-pp '$precision_pp' #end if $fail_on_refusal --output-dir out

param.name: type
param.label: Input format
param.option: Summary table with a category table (CSV)

param.name: distribution
param.label: Distribution specification
param.help: Sample size, unit, declared categories, MIC50/MIC90 with their rank convention, observed extremes and any additional counts (examples/biological_cases in the MIC-50-90 repository).

param.name: summaries
param.label: Summary table
param.help: One row per cohort and variant: cohort_id, panel_id, variant_id, n, mic50, mic90, rank_convention, rank50, rank90, minimum, maximum, iid, confidence_level.

param.name: panels
param.label: Category table
param.help: Explicit categories: panel_id, unit, category, lower, upper, lower_closed, upper_closed, panel_value.

param.name: additional_counts
param.label: Additional counts from the same sample
param.help: Optional recorded-tail counts for the same cohorts.

param.name: targets
param.label: Questions (optional)
param.help: Optional thresholds or categories to classify, with cohort_id, threshold and unit.

section.name: population
section.title: Population inference
section.help: Used only when the input declares iid sampling and a confidence level; otherwise only sample bounds are reported.

param.name: time_limit
param.label: Seconds per cohort for the time-limited searches

param.name: precision_pp
param.label: Precision of a contiguous sample description (percentage points)
param.help: Optional maximum width, written as an exact decimal such as 10.

validator.message: Enter a positive decimal number or leave empty

param.name: fail_on_refusal
param.label: Fail the job if any cohort is refused
param.help: Refused cohorts are always listed in the outputs with their reason.

has_text.text: iid sampling was not declared; no population guarantee

tool.help:
**What it does**
MIC-50-90 describes a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) distribution when a report gives only part of it: the sample size, MIC50 and MIC90 with their rank convention, observed extremes, and any exact or rounded counts. For every concentration category and range it returns the smallest and largest counts compatible with the report (sample bounds). If the input declares independent sampling (``iid: true``) and a confidence level, it also returns simultaneous population bounds.
Example: in 67 canine staphylococci tested with ampicillin, MIC50, MIC90 and the observed range allow 1-32 isolates at 0.5 mg/L. Adding the published count of 59 isolates at or below 0.25 mg/L narrows this to 2-7 isolates.
**Inputs**
- *One analysis in MIC-50-90 JSON*: see ``examples/biological_cases`` in the repository. - *Summary table with a category table*: comma-separated files as in ``examples/csv``. - *Questions* (optional): thresholds or categories whose answer should be classified.
**Outputs**
- *bounds*: one row per cohort, layer (sample, population, calibration), quantity and category, with lower and upper shares and counts. - *answers*: classification of the requested questions. - *results (JSON)* and *reusable input*: full results and the settings to repeat or extend the analysis. - *report*: the program's HTML report. Its links to the other files work after downloading all outputs into one folder.
A cohort that cannot be analysed (for example, reported values that contradict each other) is kept in the outputs with ``status = refused`` and its reason. Population results are reported as unavailable when sampling assumptions are not declared.
**More information**
Documentation: https://github.com/maciejkochanowski/mic-50-90/tree/main/docs
